signature.name: Hermitage Museum
signature.detail: One of the world's greatest art museums, housed in the Winter Palace, with vast collections from antiquity to modern art. Book tickets online to skip long queues, and go early on a weekday for fewer crowds.

signature.name: Church of the Savior on Spilled Blood
signature.detail: A stunning cathedral with colorful onion domes and intricate mosaics inside, built on the site of Alexander II's assassination. Visit in the morning to avoid crowds; modest dress is recommended.

signature.name: Peterhof Palace
signature.detail: A magnificent palace complex famous for its golden fountains and gardens, often called the 'Russian Versailles'. Take a hydrofoil from the city center in summer for a scenic arrival.

signature.name: St. Isaac's Cathedral
signature.detail: A massive gold-domed cathedral with a richly decorated interior and a colonnade offering panoramic city views. Climb the colonnade for the best photo opportunities, especially at sunset.

signature.name: Peter and Paul Fortress
signature.detail: The original citadel of St. Petersburg, housing the cathedral where Russian emperors are buried. Walk along the Neva walls for great views; the fortress is easily reached by metro.

signature.name: Nevsky Prospect
signature.detail: The main avenue of the city, lined with historic buildings, shops, and cafes, perfect for a stroll. Start at the Moscow Railway Station and walk towards the Admiralty for the full experience.

signature.name: Mariinsky Theatre
signature.detail: A world-renowned opera and ballet theater with a stunning interior. Book tickets well in advance for performances; the building is a short walk from the Sadovaya metro station.

signature.name: Bronze Horseman
signature.detail: The iconic equestrian statue of Peter the Great, a symbol of the city, located on the Neva embankment. Visit at dusk when the statue is beautifully illuminated.

signature.name: Summer Garden
signature.detail: A historic park with elegant fountains, sculptures, and shady alleys, ideal for a relaxing walk. Enter from the Neva embankment; the garden is free to visit.
